bottlenecks.reading: Scarce input: low-cost funding. SoFi's deposits grew $5.8B in Q3 2026 to $51.3B and made up 90% of average liabilities; the average deposit rate was 145 bp below warehouse facilities, about $745M of annualised interest-expense savings. A bank charter lets SoFi fund personal loans (originations $12.6B, +69% yoy) on its own balance sheet, which non-bank lenders without a charter (Upstart as a marketplace) cannot; LendingClub has a charter too. The advantage lasts as long as deposit growth keeps pricing below market funding and SoFi pays a competitive APY (10-K risk factor).

Demand side: US unsecured personal-loan balances reached a record $281B, +9.6% yoy, with originations +19.5% yoy (TransUnion Q2 2026). SoFi's personal-loan originations grew +69% yoy in Q3 2026, far faster than the market, which is share gain on the originations measure (balance-sheet vs platform split: $9.0B own balance sheet, $3.6B Loan Platform Business).

Constraint on growth: capital and credit. Faster balance-sheet lending uses capital and rests on credit quality; TransUnion shows the share of personal-loan borrowers 60+ days past due rising (3.81% vs 3.37% a year earlier per a secondary summary of the report), and the 10-K names concentration in a small number of whole-loan and Loan Platform Business purchasers whose demand can fluctuate. SoFi's personal loan charge-off rate in Q3 2026 was 2.26% as reported in the release summary (includes asset-sale effects).

Technology Platform is shrinking, not a bottleneck owner: segment net revenue fell 24% yoy to $87.4M in Q3 2026 and accounts fell 11% to 140M because a large client fully transitioned off the platform before 2025-12-31. Competitors in platform-as-a-service are only described generically in the 10-K (other technology platforms), no names, so the share reading is a gap.

Hypothesis: the limiting input for the Financial Services growth is cheap member acquisition and primary-account status (direct deposit) against Ally, Capital One, Chime, Robinhood and large banks. No attributed, comparable figure was found for competitors' deposit share, so this stays a hypothesis.

dc MGMT (statement) Original 2026 guidance assumed two rate cuts; instead one hike so far and two more expected in 2026; 2027 outlook assumes two more hikes and a 24% tax rate. Management claims equal confidence in a high-rate environment.

dc MGMT 2027 guidance is funded organically: equity capital 9.6bn supports about 71bn RWA at 13.5% (about 15bn above 56bn today) plus about 14bn from 2027 earnings plus SBC; no capital raise assumed. Total capital ratio fell 180bp in the quarter to 17.0% (CET1 16.9%) as capital is put into loans; target low-to-mid teens.

dc MGMT Targets: 100m products by end of 2030 (4x), five businesses over 1bn revenue, five over 500m, five over 100m; ROTE goal 20-30% (about 10% in Q3); NIM above 5% for the foreseeable future; fee-based revenue goal 50% of revenue (42% in Q3).

dc GUIDANCE HISTORY FY2026 adjusted net revenue: 4.655bn (2026-01-30) -> 4.655bn maintained (04-29) -> 4.75-4.85bn (07-29) -> 5.04bn (10-27), i.e. 385m above the original; EBITDA 1.6bn kept in Jan, Apr, Jul then 1.66bn; net income 825m then 840m; EPS 0.60 then 0.61. FY2025: revenue 3.200-3.275bn (01-27) -> 3.235-3.310bn (04-29) -> about 3.375bn (07-29) -> about 3.54bn (10-28); EBITDA 845-865m -> 875-895m -> about 960m -> about 1.035bn; members at least 2.8m -> 3.0m -> 3.5m. Four raises in a row in 2025; 2026 raised in two of three updates.

dc LOAN PLATFORM Q3 2026: 3.8bn originated for third parties (3.6bn personal loans; first SMB and home equity loans through the platform), 153.4m LPB revenue (151.2m from originations and referrals), up from 3.1bn and 143m in Q2. Management: monetization fluctuates with asset mix, supply and demand and partner timing. Total sold or transferred over 5.3bn in the quarter; home loans sold at 103.6%. Eighth SCLP securitization (460m, 83bp spread).

dc CREDIT Personal loan NCO 2.26% reported, about 3.4% all-in excluding late-stage delinquent loan sales (the basis to watch: reported rate flattered by delinquent loan sales); 7-8% max cumulative loss assumption, 2022Q4-2025Q4 vintages 4.71% cumulative with 33% UPB remaining versus 6.62% for 2017 vintage at same point. Student NCO 0.63%; credit card NCO 7.77%. Provision only 14.7m because most loans are at fair value (credit losses flow through fair value marks, not provision).

dc FAIR VALUE MARKS Q3: over 800m of negative fair value impact (benchmark +76bp) offset by about 734m hedge gains; personal loans marked 103.3% (down 140bp), student 101.9% (down 240bp), home 101.5%. 52.5bn of loans at fair value; rate hikes reduce marks, so earnings carry mark-to-market and hedge-effectiveness risk.

dc DEPOSITS 51.3bn (up 5.8bn in the quarter, up 37% y/y); deposits were 90% of average liabilities; deposit rate 145bp below warehouse rate, about 745m annualized interest saving. Interest expense on deposits 376m in Q3.

dc TECH PLATFORM Revenue 87.4m, down 24% y/y because a large client fully left before 2025-12-31 (customer name not disclosed here; excluding it revenue +18%); contribution margin 16% vs 28%; accounts 140m (down 11%); nine clients added year to date; management says 25% growth is the steady state. No 10% customer disclosure found in the documents read; customers list left empty.

dc FEE REVENUE Q3 fee-based revenue 570.6m (42% of revenue; Q2 39%): loan origination fees 270.9m (2.6x), loan platform fees 151.2m, interchange 49.7m (+77%), brokerage 18.0m, technology services 52.4m. Crypto net revenue 1.6m (gross 161.6m less cost 160.0m).

dc ACCOUNTING Product counts are cumulative (include repaid loans) and the product definition was widened in Q1-Q3 2026 (Invest now six sub-products incl. Composer, SoFi Plus, Smart Card, credit card with personal loan rollover; prior periods not recast); treat products growth as partly definitional. Adjusted net revenue excludes servicing-rights and residual-interest valuation changes (net -14.0m in Q3). Q3 10-Q not yet filed (call says next month), so Q3 numbers are from the release only; quarter_case.json is built on the release, not on companyfacts (the prefetch's companyfacts revenue line of 153.6m is a partial XBRL tag, not total revenue).

dc EQUITY Book value 11.3bn (8.71 per share), tangible book 9.7bn (7.48 per share, up 25% y/y); 1,296.6m shares outstanding, diluted weighted 1,357.8m; 2026 convertible notes settlement mentioned in the Q1 release. Debt 3.86bn (up from 1.82bn at 2025 year-end). Cash 2.81bn plus restricted 0.79bn, investment securities 4.99bn.
dc RISK (10-K Item 1A, 'Risks Related to Market and Interest Rates') Interest-rate sensitivity: fair value of 52bn of loans, NIM and demand react to rates and funding costs.

dc RISK (10-K Item 1A) Credit: 'If we do not make accurate credit and pricing decisions or effectively forecast our loss rates, our business and financial results will be harmed'; a personal loan book of about 32bn fair value is unsecured and consumer-cycle sensitive.

dc RISK (10-K Item 1A, 'Risks Related to Funding and Liquidity') Deposit-based funding and balance-sheet management, warehouse covenants, and capital needs to support growth; loan sale and securitization market access (Loan Platform Business depends on third-party buyers).
dc RISK (10-K Item 1A) Bank regulation: SoFi is a bank holding company; OCC/Fed/CFPB supervision, capital requirements, unsafe-or-unsound conduct and consumer-protection exposure.
dc RISK (10-K Item 1A) Member acquisition and competition: growth depends on retaining and attracting members and on brand and marketing spend (sales and marketing 444m in Q3, up 55% y/y).
dc RISK (10-K Item 1A) History of losses before Q4 2023: profitability is recent (12 profitable quarters) and valuation of new products (crypto, SoFiUSD, business banking) is unproven.
dc RISK Technology Platform client concentration and attrition: the large-client exit cut segment revenue 24% and margin to 16%.

market_direction.reading: Demand grows but the macro turned against lenders. US unsecured personal-loan balances reached a record $281B (+9.6% yoy) with originations +19.5% yoy (TransUnion Q2 2026). Rates went the wrong way for SoFi: a quarter-point Fed hike in September 2026 and a hold at 3.75-4.00% on 2026-10-28 with a further hike priced. Labour is softening (September unemployment 4.2%, payrolls +29k) and 4.7% of household debt is in some stage of delinquency (NY Fed 2026Q2). A tailwind on capital rules: the March 2026 Basel III re-proposal estimates lower CET1 requirements for smaller banks (final rule not yet confirmed).

bottleneck_potential.reading: SoFi is not an industry bottleneck; it owns a cost advantage on the scarce input of the lending business, cheap stable funding. Deposits are $51.3B (+$5.8B in Q3 2026), 90% of average liabilities, priced 145 bp below warehouse lines (about $745M a year of interest saved). Marketplace lenders without a charter (Upstart) cannot fund on balance sheet; LendingClub, Ally and Capital One have the same charter-funding advantage, so it is a moat versus non-banks, not a bottleneck. It lasts while deposit growth keeps pricing below market funding; the shift to time deposits (higher cost) is the erosion signal to watch.

share_trajectory.reading: SoFi is taking share in lending and deposits and losing it in the technology platform. Personal-loan originations $12.6B in Q3 2026 (+69% yoy) against market originations +19.5%; Lending segment adjusted revenue $807.4M vs $481.4M a year earlier, against LendingClub interest income +15.1% and Upstart revenue +41.8% (Q2 2026). Deposits +37% yoy while Ally's FY2025 revenue fell 3.3%. Financial Services revenue $525.1M (+25%) outgrows Robinhood's total revenue (+11.8% in Q3 2026) from a smaller base. Technology Platform revenue fell to $87.4M from $114.6M (-24%) after a large client left. Bases differ (SoFi net revenue vs competitors' XBRL lines): direction only.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than LendingClub and Upstart on scale and funding (a $51.3B deposit base; $16.9B quarterly originations). Against Capital One: lower NIM (6.14% vs 8.41%) but more capital (CET1 16.9% vs 13.8%). Weaker than all large peers on returns: ROTE about 10% in Q3 2026 against management's own 20-30% goal. Against Robinhood in investing and cash management SoFi is smaller and less profitable (Robinhood Q3 2026 net income $468M on $1,424M revenue; SoFi total net income $241M on $1,385M). The edge is breadth (17.1M members, 1.56 products per member) rather than a best-in-class single product.

threats.reading: 1) Rates: about $1.4B of fair-value premium on $52.5B of fair-value loans; Q3 2026 benchmark +76 bp caused more than $800M of negative marks, offset by about $734M of hedge gains (call), and further hikes repeat this. 2) Capital: CET1 fell to 16.9% (22.8% at end-2025) as risk-weighted assets grew to $56.2B; management targets low-to-mid teens and says 2027 needs no raise, but faster growth or losses would force slower growth or new equity. 3) Credit: unsecured book in a softening labour market; credit-card NCO 7.77%. 4) Loan Platform Business depends on a small number of third-party buyers (10-K). 5) Robinhood moving into banking and cards for the same young customers. 6) Technology Platform client attrition (-24% revenue). 7) Bank supervision (OCC/Fed/CFPB) and capital rules.

bear.event_he: עליית ריבית או התרחבות מרווחי אשראי מוחקת חלק גדול מהפרמיה של כ-1.4 מיליארד דולר על שווי ההלוואות (תוספת של אחוז בריבית = כמיליארד דולר לפני גידור).
הפסדי האשראי בהלוואות האישיות חוזרים לכ-4.4% (במקום כ-3.4% היום), וההנחה של שיעור החדלות כבר עולה שלושה רבעונים ברצף.
יחס ההון (CET1) ממשיך לרדת כ-2 נקודות ברבעון; סופיי מאטה את הצמיחה או מגייסת הון שוב, כמו בגיוסים של 2025 ב-20.85 ו-27.50 דולר.
הכנסות פלטפורמת ההלוואות והפלטפורמה הטכנולוגית ממשיכות לרדת, וההוצאה על שיווק (כ-55%+) אוכלת את הצמיחה.

base.event_he: סופיי מסיימת את 2026 סביב התחזית (הכנסות כ-5.04 מיליארד, רווח כ-840 מיליון) ומספקת ב-2027 הכנסות של כ-6.4 מיליארד ורווח של כ-1.28 מיליארד.
מספר החברים והמוצרים ממשיך לגדול (17.1 מיליון חברים, +36%) והפיקדונות הזולים ממשיכים לממן את ההלוואות.
התשואה על ההון עולה בהדרגה לכ-10.5%-11% ב-2028, בהתאם ליעד צמיחת הרווח למניה של 38%-42% בשנה.

bull.event_he: סופיי שוב מכה ומעלה את התחזית: רווח 2027 מעל 1.28 מיליארד, כמו ההכאות של 13%-23% ב-EBITDA בשנים האחרונות.
הכנסות מעמלות (42% מההכנסות היום) גדלות מהר יותר מספר ההלוואות, כך שהרווח עולה בלי לצרוך הרבה הון.
הרווח למניה צומח בקצב העליון של היעד (42% בשנה עד 2028) והתשואה על ההון מגיעה לכ-16% עד 2031.

bear.reason_he: זה בנק, ולכן התשואה הנמדדת היא על ההון העצמי (כולל מוניטין), לא ROIC. ב-2025 היא הייתה 5.7%, וברבעון השלישי של 2026 כ-8.6% בקצב שנתי. בתרחיש הדובי היא נשארת סביב 7.5%: יחס ההון (CET1) יורד בכ-2 נקודות ברבעון, ולכן צריך למכור יותר הלוואות או לגייס הון. בנוסף, ריבית ומרווחי אשראי גבוהים שוחקים את פרמיית השווי ההוגן של ההלוואות. תשואה מתחת לעלות ההון פירושה שכל דולר שמושקע בצמיחה שווה פחות מדולר, ולכן המכפיל נמוך.

base.reason_he: התשואה על ההון עלתה מ-5.7% ב-2025 לכ-8.6% היום (על ההון המוחשי, בלי מוניטין, כ-10%). תחזית ההנהלה ל-2027, רווח של 1.28 מיליארד דולר על הון של כ-12-13 מיליארד, משתמעת לכ-10-11% על ההון הממוצע. ההון החדש שמושקע בצמיחה מרוויח יותר מהממוצע בזכות מינוף תפעולי. להנהלה יש רקורד של העלאת התחזית בכל רבעון ב-2025-2026. לכן 12% הם המסלול הסביר, מעט מעל עלות ההון: מכפיל מתון שיורד עם האטת הצמיחה.

bull.reason_he: יעד ההנהלה הוא צמיחה של 38-42% בשנה ברווח למניה בשנים 2025-2028. אם זה קורה בלי גיוס הון נוסף, התשואה על ההון מגיעה לאמצע העשרות (כ-16%). לשם כך צריך יותר הכנסות מעמלות (פלטפורמת ההלוואות, מוצרים לכל לקוח) והוצאות שיווק שגדלות לאט יותר מההכנסות. Ally, מתחרה ישיר בפיקדונות, מרוויחה כבר היום 13.1% על ההון המוחשי. זה עדיין לא הוכח, ולכן המכפיל הגבוה מותנה.

key_risk.reading_he: הסיכון המרכזי הוא שהרווח וההון של סופיי תלויים בשווי ההוגן של ההלוואות: פרמיה של כ-1.4 מיליארד דולר (כ-14% מההון המוחשי) נשחקה ב-630 מיליון ברבעון אחד, ותוספת של אחוז לריבית מורידה כמיליארד דולר לפני גידור, בזמן שיחס ההון יורד כ-2 נקודות ברבעון.

moat.note: Evidenced source: charter-based deposit funding 145 bp below warehouse (about $745M a year) versus non-bank Upstart; LendingClub, Ally and Capital One share it, so it is not unique. Brand and member scale are not separately evidenced.

switching_costs.note: Products per member 1.56 (1.47 a year earlier) and about half of new products from existing members show cross-sell; product counts are cumulative and the definition was widened in 2026, so part of the growth is definitional. Deposits are rate-sensitive (time deposits growing), which limits lock-in.

pricing_power.note: Financial Services revenue per product $90 vs $104 a year earlier: product growth (+44%) outruns monetisation (+25%). Deposits require a competitive APY (10-K). Lending risk-adjusted margin (7.6% core personal loans) is healthy but set by credit and funding, not pricing power.

customer_concentration.note: Consumers are diverse; concentration sits in the Loan Platform Business buyers (10-K: a small number of purchasers, $3.8B originated for them in Q3 2026) and in the Technology Platform, where one client's exit cut segment revenue 24%.

market_size.note: US unsecured personal loans $281B, 26.9M borrowers, growing; SoFi's balance-sheet loans at fair value $52.5B across personal, student and home leaves room, plus deposits and investing.

competition.note: Crowded field (LendingClub, Upstart, Robinhood, Ally, Capital One, large banks) but SoFi is growing faster than each on the available lines; the 10-K names only competitor classes.

substitutes.note: Credit cards substitute for personal loans and brokerages/neobanks for Money and Invest; no evidence of a substitute taking SoFi's volume yet.

management.note: Revenue guidance raised every quarter in 2025 and 2026 (FY2026 $4.655B -> $5.04B) despite a rate hike instead of the two assumed cuts; caveat: EPS guidance only $0.60 -> $0.61 because the extra revenue is reinvested. CEO open-market purchases in 2026 (aggregator, not verified on EDGAR).

capital_allocation.note: Equity raised in 2025 at $20.85 and $27.50 (above today's ~$17), shares +18% since Dec-24; SBC $220M in 9M 2026 (about 2% a year dilution), no buybacks. ROIC unavailable in the forensic screen; ROTE about 10% sits near or below a high-beta bank's cost of equity, so growth is not yet clearly value-creating. Most of the TBV/share rise came from raises, not earnings.

regulation.note: Bank holding company under OCC/Fed/CFPB; Basel re-proposal would lower capital requirements (not final); federal student-loan changes (RAP) have an unclear effect on refinance demand.

technology_ai.note: Owns its stack (Galileo/Technisys), but the platform shrank to $87.4M revenue and 140M accounts (-11%), margin 16% vs 28%; no evidenced AI-driven advantage.

geopolitics.note: Low exposure: 93.1% of FY2025 revenue in the US, no supply-chain or export-control exposure.

cyclical.reason: Growth is member, product and deposit share gain (members +36%, products +44%, deposits +37% y/y) and revenue guidance was raised through a year that brought a rate hike instead of the two cuts assumed; the consumer-credit cycle enters through the ROE path of the bear (fair-value marks and charge-offs), not as a revenue peak.

base.terminal_reason: A deposit franchise of 17.1m members funding loans at 1.45pp below warehouse funding, products per member rising (1.56) and a NIM guided above 5%: a modest edge of about 0.3pp over the cost of equity is kept, far below today's lending spreads.
base.reason: Start 9.5%: Q3 2026 annualised ROE 8.6% (ROTE 10%), normalised upward for the $10.9m after-tax servicing-rights fair-value charge and toward the FY2027 guide (net income $1.28bn on an average book of about $12.4bn = about 10.3%, computed). Year 5 12.5%: the 2025-2028 EPS CAGR target of 38-42% and the EBITDA margin rising to 35% imply ROE of about 10.5-11% in 2028 (computed); continuing operating leverage (net income margin from about 17% in 2026 to 20% in 2027) takes it to about 12.5% by 2031. Book growth 9.5% = all profit retained (payout 0); the engine keeps shares constant at the point-in-time count, and SBC (about $290m a year) is a cost inside GAAP net income, so dilution from awards is charged. Past raises are in the opening share count.

bear.reason: Start 6%: back to the FY2025 ROE of 5.7%. Mechanisms, sized from SoFi's own filings: (1) fair value - the remaining loan premium is about $1.4bn and a +100bp move cost $1,040.8m before hedges (June 2026 10-Q); losing about half of the premium after tax is about 5% of book; (2) credit - the personal-loan default assumption already rose 4.57% to 5.10%, and an all-in NCO back at the 4.4% of late 2025 on about $31bn of personal loans costs about $300m a year pre-tax; (3) funding/capital - CET1 fell 22.8% to 16.9% in three quarters with RWA +68%, so growth is cut to what retained profit funds (book growth 5%) or new equity is issued below today's price. ROE recovers only to 8.5%, below the cost of equity, also at the terminal.

bull.terminal_reason: A national digital bank with a cheap deposit base (1.45pp below warehouse funding), 42% fee-based revenue that needs little capital and products per member rising: part of the excess return survives competition (Ally, Capital One, Nu) at about 2pp over the cost of equity.
bull.reason: Start 10%: the FY2027 guide (net income $1.28bn, about 10.3% on average book, computed) reached early, consistent with EBITDA beats of 13-23% against guidance. Year 5 16% (ROTE about 18%): the top of the 38-42% EPS CAGR target to 2028 sustained by fee revenue (42% of revenue) growing faster than the capital-consuming loan book, NIM held above the guided 5% floor and marketing growing slower than revenue. Book growth 10% = all profit retained.

regulatory_capital.reason: SoFi Technologies risk-weighted assets $48.68bn at June 30, 2026 and the CET1 requirement of 7.0% including the 2.5% capital conservation buffer, from the 10-Q capital table. The Q3 release shows RWA already at $56.24bn (Sep 30, 2026; CET1 16.9%), so this filing figure understates the current requirement by about 15%.
